task: Hiring funnel data for a role open 8 weeks: 120 applicants -> 40 phone-screened -> 8 onsite -> 1 offer -> declined. Industry benchmark for this role is offer-accept rate ~70%. Diagnose the most likely cause of the decline and the single highest-leverage fix -- the data points to a specific funnel stage, not 'improve the whole process.'
rubric: Score 0-1 on: (a) correctly identifies that the funnel stages before the offer look healthy (120->40->8 is a reasonable screen-to-onsite ratio) so the problem is specifically the offer stage itself (comp, timeline, competing offer, candidate experience during the process), not sourcing or screening; (b) does not recommend 'source more candidates' or 'screen more thoroughly' as the primary fix, since that doesn't address a single declined offer; (c) proposes a specific, testable hypothesis for the decline (e.g. comp below market, slow process losing the candidate to a competitor, poor onsite experience) rather than a vague 'find out why.'
